newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore firms invest S$676 mln in manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore firms invest S$676 mln in manufacturing.

text.p: Singapore's 200 so-called Promising Local Enterprises (PLEs) more than doubled their investment in new plants and machinery in 1996, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Friday.
It said in a statement they spent Singapore $676 million in 1996 in new plants, machinery and other manufacturing facilities -- an increase of 140 percent.
In addition, PLE Companies in the services sector chalked up S$302 million in business spending in 1996, it said.
The EDB said it had identified more than 200 PLEs -- companies deemed to have entrepreneurship qualities and leadership in their sectors, strong growth potential and a desire to do business overseas.
EDB said that in line with the slower economic growth in 1996, turnover growth among the PLEs was a moderate 20 percent compared to 30 percent in 1995.
Average sales per company rose to S$40 million from S$33 million in 1995.
The EDB is aiming to help 100 PLEs reach the S$100 million sales target by 2005. By 1996, 20 PLEs had reached the mark, it said.
The EDB helps PLEs with financial, manpower resources and provides tax incentives, grants and business development contacts.
It said total venture capital funds in Singapore to support growth of local enterprises rose 7.7 percent to S$7.86 billion in January 1997 from a year ago.
